layers.name: Core Framework
layers.description: Base classes, framework infrastructure, expression parser, serial I/O, and utility libraries that all other layers depend on. Includes tools/ (JVSMain, Gatter, CustomAnalogComp, Expression, Scanner), MyParser/, VisualLogic/, and root-level framework utilities.

layers.name: Circuit Elements
layers.description: Visual programming elements representing circuit/logic diagram nodes: analog processing, boolean gates, bit operations, math/numeric, string, 1D arrays/vectors, canvas, color, comparison, display, events/timers, file I/O, flowcharts, signal generators, group/ungroup, thread, error handling, decorators, automation (Fuzzy, PID), microcontroller programming (MCU), sub-elements, system operations, and external interfaces (email, UDP, JFreeChart, media, joystick, keyboard, monitor). Sorted under CircuitElements/.

layers.name: Front Panel Elements
layers.description: UI front panel components for building graphical user interfaces in MyOpenLab: industrial automation panels, boolean indicators/controls, decorators, charts/graph displays, numeric displays/sliders, input elements, output displays, and version 2.0 variants. Located under FrontElements/ (excluding Drivers/).

layers.name: Hardware Drivers
layers.description: Hardware interface drivers for physical devices: HC-06 Bluetooth module, scroll saw, OpenCV computer vision, robot arm kinematics, 2WD robotic platform servo control, Skat card game controller, and TinkerForge industrial modules. Located under FrontElements/Drivers/.

layers.name: Code Generation Backends
layers.description: Virtual machines and compiler toolchains that translate MyOpenLab visual programs into executable code for various targets: Arduino (AVR C), ATmega168/328 (bare-metal C), PIC 16F877 (C), Java VM, and VisualLogic runtime versions 1-7 with their element models and XML parsers. Located under VirtualMachines/.

layers.name: Templates

layers.name: Documentation

layers.name: Configuration

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The Elements library is organized as a MyOpenLab distribution with root-level configuration (update.txt version tracking, config.txt captions), a Documentations directory with multi-language (DE/EN/ES) descriptions and XML metadata manifests, and top-level element directories. Start here to understand the project structure and packaging conventions.

tour.title: Core Framework: JVSMain Base Class
tour.description: JVSMain is the abstract base class that every MyOpenLab circuit element extends. It defines the element lifecycle (init, process, start, paint, loadFromStream, saveToStream), pin management (initInputPins, initOutputPins), property editors, and the VisualLogic integration contract. Understanding JVSMain is essential for grasping how all elements work.

tour.title: Core Framework: Execution Flow and Gate Base Classes
tour.description: MainFlow and MCUMainFlow orchestrate element execution during simulation, while Gatter/Gatter2/Gatter3 are reusable base classes for boolean logic gates with 2-input, multi-input, and clock-delay variants respectively. These form the backbone of the simulation engine and logic gate hierarchy.

tour.title: Circuit Elements
tour.description: The CircuitElements directory contains hundreds of visual programming nodes organized by category: boolean logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR), bitwise operations, math/numeric (add, subtract, multiply, trig, filters), analog signal processing (FFT, DCT, generators, triggers), automation (PID, Fuzzy Logic), string operations, 1D arrays/vectors, display drivers, event/timer components, file I/O, and interfaces (email, UDP, charts, media, joystick). Each element extends JVSMain and follows a consistent pattern of initInputPins/initOutputPins/process.

tour.title: Front Panel Elements
tour.description: The FrontElements directory provides UI components for building graphical front panels: gauges, numeric displays, sliders (H-V-Slider), boolean indicators (light bulbs, switches), oscilloscopes (XY, strip-chart), bar charts, compasses, 2D decorators (ellipse, labels, images), and chart widgets. These elements render interactive or display-only panels that bind to circuit variables for real-time visualization.

tour.title: Code Generation Backends
tour.description: The VirtualMachines directory contains compiler toolchains that translate MyOpenLab visual programs into executable C code for microcontrollers (Arduino/AVR, ATmega168/328, PIC 16F877) and a Java VM runtime. Each compiler follows the same architecture: tokenizer, parser, stack interpreter, and C code emitter. The VisualLogic versions (1-7) provide the runtime VM for executing visual programs on the desktop.

tour.title: Expression Parser and Scanner
tour.description: The Expression class and Scanner tokenizer implement a mathematical expression evaluator used by elements to parse user-defined formulas at runtime. The MyParser/Parser provides a separate recursive-descent parser for the MyOpenLab visual logic expression language. These components enable dynamic computation without hardcoded logic.
